title: The goal isn't to win the argument. It's to get into the training data.
body: Drop Site News reports that Brad Parscale, Trump's former campaign manager, is running a $46.5 million operation to shape what AI chatbots tell you about Gaza. His firm, Clock Tower X, built a network of 10 websites that dress up Israeli talking points as news and fact-checking. One of them, FactSignal.org, calls itself a fact-checker while denying the genocide in Gaza and discrediting Palestinian journalists.

Here's the most interesting bit, the sites are not trying to go viral, they are trying to get crawled. Common Crawl, the open web archive that feeds most major AI models, scooped up the network 912 times between January and June. In January it happened twice. By May it was 376 times. Drop Site's tests found the content already surfacing in Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot, with traces in Perplexity too.
This is manufacturing consent built for the machine age. You do not need to convince a person anymore. You just need to be sitting in the training data when they ask the bot.
